title: Supreme Court keeps Azam Khan's forgery conviction on hold, extends relief to wife and son
dek: The court dismissed Uttar Pradesh's appeal and suspended the convictions of Tazeen Fatma and Abdullah Azam Khan too. Khan remains in custody in a separate money-laundering case.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Supreme Court on Tuesday upheld the suspension of Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan's conviction in the forged birth certificate case involving his son, and gave the same relief to his wife, Tazeen Fatma, and son, Abdullah Azam Khan, according to legal reports.

A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu dismissed the Uttar Pradesh government's appeal against an Allahabad High Court order of May 2024 that had stayed Mr Khan's conviction, and allowed the appeals of Ms Fatma and Mr Abdullah Azam Khan, whose convictions the High Court had refused to stay. "The Court today dismissed the State's appeal and allowed the appeal by the wife and son," one legal report said. The judgment had been reserved on 28 October. Its full text had not been published on the court's website by early Tuesday afternoon, so the court's reasoning is not yet known.

## The case

The case began with a complaint by Akash Saxena, now a BJP MLA from Rampur, who alleged that Abdullah Azam Khan held two birth certificates with different dates of birth, 1 January 1993 and 30 September 1990. The prosecution said the second was used to show he was old enough to contest the 2017 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election.

On 18 October 2023 a Rampur court convicted all three of cheating, forgery and criminal conspiracy and sentenced each to seven years in prison. After their appeals failed, they went to the Allahabad High Court in revision. On 24 May 2024, the High Court suspended all three sentences and granted bail, but stayed only Mr Khan's conviction. It said his role was different from that of his wife and son, since there was no material showing he had supplied information for the second certificate, whereas Ms Fatma had applied for it without disclosing the first and Mr Abdullah Azam Khan had used it in his nomination and other documents, according to legal reports.

A stay on a conviction, unlike a suspended sentence, can matter for elected office: under the Representation of the People Act, a lawmaker sentenced to two years or more is disqualified from the date of conviction, and a stay by an appeal court can lift that disqualification. Whether Tuesday's order affects any past disqualification was not addressed in the reports.

## Still in custody

The ruling does not free Mr Khan. He was arrested by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) in a money-laundering case linked to the Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust minutes after he and his son walked out of Rampur jail on bail in a separate case at the end of October. On 5 November the Supreme Court declined to hear his challenge to that arrest and sent it to the Allahabad High Court.

On Monday, a High Court bench of Justices Rajiv Gupta and Devendra Singh gave no interim relief and asked the ED to file an affidavit within a week on whether it had served notice before the arrest and followed the mandatory legal procedure, according to reports. Arguing for Mr Khan, senior advocate Kapil Sibal alleged political vendetta and said the grounds of arrest were not given to Mr Khan. For the ED, Additional Solicitor General SV Raju said five contemporaneous documents, including a panchnama and a video recording, showed Mr Khan was repeatedly asked to read and accept the grounds of arrest and refused. A special court in Ghaziabad has extended his remand until 26 November, reports said.

Mr Khan, a former Uttar Pradesh minister, faces 92 criminal cases, the Allahabad High Court noted in a recent bail order.

## What happens next

The High Court hearing on the ED arrest continues, with the ED's affidavit due within a week. The Supreme Court's written judgment, once uploaded, will set out its reasons.
